subject: Request to annualize additional capacity midterm and invoicing options
messages:
From: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@acuomedical.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acuomedical.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity increase — options and co-term?

Hi Tessa,

Hope you're well. We're launching a pilot for a new clinical decision-support flow and expect to need another 1.2M inference units per month starting Sept 1 — roughly a 30% bump to our current committed capacity. We're mid-year on our annual contract and want to avoid creating multiple invoices or hitting disproportionate uplift rates.

Questions:
- Can we add that capacity mid-contract and have the additional units annualized to our Jan renewal date?
- What discount rates apply for midterm top-ups vs full-year uplifts?
- Will Redwood allow a single amended invoice or do you require a separate midterm invoice?

Procurement (cc'd) will need an outline of invoicing and PO wording if we move forward.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

— Liam
Director, Platform Engineering
Acuo Medical
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@acuomedical.com>
Cc: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@acuomedical.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — options and co-term?

Hi Liam — great to hear about the pilot, congrats.

Short answers up front: yes, we can add capacity mid-contract; there are two common approaches and a straightforward invoicing path. I'll summarize below and attach a draft amendment for procurement. Ben and Kim are CC'd with the pricing and billing details.

Option A — Annualize (preferred for predictable unit economics):
- Add the 1.2M units immediately; we annualize the additional annual equivalent to align with your Jan renewal.
- One amended commitment line on your contract (amendment) that increases committed units for the remainder of the contract period, annualized to the renewal date.
- Pricing: blended uplift rate — a modest midterm uplift factor (we propose 10% uplift on the marginal units) vs a full-year add-on discount.
- Invoicing: single amendment invoice for the pro-rated portion now, then the annualized bump reflected in the Jan invoice (no duplicate billing for the same months).

Option B — Temporary top-up (if you want to trial):
- Billed as a usage top-up at standard overage rates (higher unit price) with the option to convert to Option A before Jan.

I've attached a short proposal and a draft amendment with suggested PO language. Ben — can you confirm the numbers if we apply a 10% blended uplift on the 1.2M marginal units?

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min call with procurement and finance to walk the invoice flow.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: RDW_Acuo_proposal_v2.pdf, amendment_draft.docx
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Rourke <liam.orourke@acuomedical.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity increase — options and co-term?

Quick math and recommended pricing approach:

Assumptions:
- Current committed units: 4.0M/mo (example)
- Requested bump: +1.2M/mo starting 2026-09-01
- Remaining term to Jan renewal: 5 months (Sep–Jan inclusive)

Recommended: Blended uplift — convert added capacity to annualized commitment at a 10% uplift on marginal units for the remaining term, then full annual pricing at renewal. That yields a lower immediate cost vs pure overage and preserves your priority capacity.

Example pricing line (illustrative):
- Midterm amendment: 1.2M units annualized to Jan renewal priced at $0.012/unit * 0.9 (10% uplift) for pro-rate window -> pro-rated invoice amount: $X (see pricing_breakdown.csv).
- If Acuo prefers to lock full-year discount now, we can apply the renewal tier pricing and backfill pro-rata — I'm including both numbers in the CSV.

I'll flag to billing that procurement will need a single amendment invoice showing the pro-rated charge + statement of the new annualized commitment. Kim — i'll let you confirm billing language and PO requirements.

— Ben
Senior Account Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: pricing_breakdown.csv

Hi Tessa / Ben,

Thanks for the proposal. Procurement has two clarifying requests before we can issue a PO:
1) We need the amendment to show a single invoice for the pro-rated charge (no separate midterm monthly invoices).
2) Please provide exact PO language and the final dollar amounts for the pro-rated invoice so we can route for internal approval.

Also confirm whether the annualized bump will be treated as a recurring contract commitment (i.e., will appear on the Jan renewal as a committed line). If so we need the renewal line item id in the amendment.

We prefer DocuSign for signature.

Procurement
Acuo Medical

Hi — thanks for the clear list. See answers inline and attached final amendment for signature.

1) Invoice flow: we will issue a single pro-rated invoice for the midterm charge covering Sep–Dec prorated amount (invoice will be dated upon signing). No separate monthly midterm invoices.
2) PO language (copy/paste friendly):
"Purchase Order for mid-contract amendment RDW-56842: Acuo Medical authorizes Redwood Inference to increase committed usage by 1,200,000 inference units per month, effective 2026-09-01. The pro-rated charge for the remainder of the current contract term will be billed as a single invoice upon execution. Annualized commitment and pricing will be reflected at renewal on 2027-01-01."

Attached: amendment_draft.docx (signed-ready), RDW_Acuo_proposal_v2.pdf (final numbers), pricing_breakdown.csv (detailed math).

We will issue the DocuSign link once you confirm the preferred signer name and email. For transparency, Ben has left the two pricing options in the CSV; our recommended path is the blended 10% uplift on marginal units.

If you confirm signer details by EOD tomorrow we'll route DocuSign today and can get you on the new capacity by 9/1.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
